criteria.name: Statement of the Case (written advocacy)
criteria.description: Drafts a clear, well-organized, persuasive arbitration statement of the case that frames the issues, marshals the facts, and states the requested relief.

subcriteria.name: Issue framing
subcriteria.description: Frames the retaliation and unpaid-wage issues for the arbitral forum with a coherent theory.

subcriteria.name: Fact marshaling
subcriteria.description: Organizes the record evidence — timeline, documents, and witnesses — into a persuasive factual narrative.

subcriteria.name: Requested relief and remedy
subcriteria.description: States and supports the relief sought (reinstatement or back/front pay, unpaid wages, reference).

criteria.name: Fact development and witness interviews
criteria.description: Investigates and develops the facts through the client and fact witnesses and builds a defensible chronology from the documents.

subcriteria.name: Client interview
subcriteria.description: Conducts an effective client interview that earns trust and surfaces sensitive, rapport-gated facts.

subcriteria.name: Fact-witness interviews
subcriteria.description: Interviews corroborating witnesses and identifies represented persons who may not be contacted directly.

subcriteria.name: Chronology and documents
subcriteria.description: Builds and maintains an accurate chronology tied to the documentary record.

criteria.name: Case theory and legal analysis
criteria.description: Develops a sound retaliation / wrongful-discharge theory and analyzes the enforceability posture of the arbitration agreement.

criteria.name: Arbitration hearing advocacy
criteria.description: Presents the case at the arbitration hearing through opening, examination, and closing.

subcriteria.name: Opening and closing
subcriteria.description: Delivers a focused opening statement and a persuasive closing argument.

subcriteria.name: Direct and cross-examination
subcriteria.description: Conducts effective direct of the client and corroborating witnesses and cross of adverse witnesses.

criteria.name: Professional responsibility and counseling
criteria.description: Handles the Rule 4.2 no-contact issue correctly and counsels the client on settlement versus proceeding.
